mr_title: perf(label): reduce the time of calling lv_text_get_size when drawing

expected_issues.title: The change replaces dynamic text width calculation with a cached value (`dsc->text_size.x…
expected_issues.description: The change replaces dynamic text width calculation with a cached value (`dsc->text_size.x`), risking incorrect rendering if text updates occur without refreshing the cache. Ensure the cached dimensions remain consistent with the current text state.
expected_issues.source_text: The change replaces dynamic text width calculation with a cached value (`dsc->text_size.x`), risking incorrect rendering if text updates occur without refreshing the cache. Ensure the cached dimensions remain consistent with the current text state.

expected_issues.title: `label->text_size` is reused later for scroll alignment/scroll-circular logic, but it’s o…
expected_issues.description: `label->text_size` is reused later for scroll alignment/scroll-circular logic, but it’s only updated in `lv_label_refr_text()`. If font/letter_space/line_space/flags/max_w or `label->text` change and `lv_label_refr_text()` is not called before `draw_main()`, `text_size` can become stale and cause wrong alignment/scroll behavior. Consider either recomputing size in the specific draw paths when needed, or ensure all setters that impact text metrics update `label->text_size` (or invalidate and trigger `lv_label_refr_text()`) before draw.

Consider either recomputing size in the specific draw paths when needed, or ensure all setters that impact text metrics update `label->text_size` (or invalidate and trigger `lv_label_refr_text()`) before draw.

expected_issues.title: `label->text_size` is updated here based on current `max_w` and flags
expected_issues.description: `label->text_size` is updated here based on current `max_w` and flags. If other code paths compute size with a different `max_w` (e.g., `LV_COORD_MAX` used in scroll checks previously), reusing this cached value can change behavior. Verify that `label->text_size` is intended to represent the unbounded width (`LV_COORD_MAX`) size for scrolling decisions; otherwise consider caching both constrained and unconstrained sizes or keep the local `lv_text_get_size(... LV_COORD_MAX ...)` for scroll logic.

expected_issues.title: The newly added `text_size` struct member is uninitialized, risking undefined behavior if…
expected_issues.description: The newly added `text_size` struct member is uninitialized, risking undefined behavior if accessed before `lv_label_refr_text` sets it; initialize to `{0, 0}` during label creation.
expected_issues.source_text: The newly added `text_size` struct member is uninitialized, risking undefined behavior if accessed before `lv_label_refr_text` sets it; initialize to `{0, 0}` during label creation.

expected_issues.title: The new text_size field is not consistently updated when the cache is invalidated
expected_issues.description: The new text_size field is not consistently updated when the cache is invalidated. In LV_EVENT_GET_SELF_SIZE handler, when invalid_size_cache is true, only size_cache gets updated but text_size remains stale. This creates inconsistency between the two cached size fields.
expected_issues.source_text: The new text_size field is not consistently updated when the cache is invalidated. In LV_EVENT_GET_SELF_SIZE handler, when invalid_size_cache is true, only size_cache gets updated but text_size remains stale. This creates inconsistency between the two cached size fields.

known_false_positives.description: The assignment to `label->text_size` must be triggered for every label text modification; verify all text-changing code paths invoke `lv_label_refr_text` to prevent stale size values during rendering.
